name: Jeffrey Hessekiel
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Cytokinetics (since Nov 2025)
profile: Biopharma lawyer who was EVP & General Counsel of Exelixis from 2014 to 2025, leading 100+ legal, IP, compliance, quality and government-affairs staff. Earlier he spent a decade at Gilead (ending as Chief Compliance & Quality Officer) and was Senior Counsel at Arnold & Porter. In November 2025 he joined Cytokinetics as EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer.
interesting_fact: Before law school he worked with international nongovernmental organizations; he went on to hold legal roles at Wilson Sonsini and Heller Ehrman before moving in-house at Gilead in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of HairToStay, a nonprofit that helps cancer patients afford scalp cooling to preserve their hair during chemotherapy, as well as Biocom California and Life Sciences Cares. Duke political science BA; GWU Law JD.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low public profile. Cytokinetics media/IR contact in 2026 releases is Diane Weiser, SVP Corporate Affairs (company line published in releases, e.g. https://ir.cytokinetics.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Cytokinetics-to-Participate-in-June-Investor-Conferences/default.aspx).

name: L Reade Fahs
current_role: Executive Chairman, National Vision Holdings (America's Best, Eyeglass World)
profile: Optical-retail veteran who led National Vision as CEO for 23 years (2002 to Aug 2025), building the discount eyewear chain behind America's Best and Eyeglass World and taking it public in 2017. Before that he spent a decade at LensCrafters and ran Vision Express in the UK. Since August 2025 he has been Executive Chairman, with Alex Wilkes as CEO.
interesting_fact: He chaired VisionSpring for a decade and has sat on RestoringVision's board for ~20 years; the company says the two nonprofits have provided eyeglasses to over 30 million low-income people worldwide during his tenure.
deep_cut_fact: Between LensCrafters/Vision Express and National Vision he was CEO of First Tuesday, the European dot-com era internet start-up/network. He started at LensCrafters in 1986 in advertising and new product development, and holds a Harvard BA in English and American Literature.
notes: Also on boards of PetVet Care Centers (KKR), Atlanta Committee for Progress and Alliance Theatre; active with the Coalition for Clear Vision. Emails taken from release boilerplate (could not re-fetch page directly).

name: Richard Scott Struthers
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals (acquired by Vertex, Sept 2026); Chairman, Radionetics Oncology
profile: Endocrinologist-turned-founder (PhD, UC San Diego) who co-founded Crinetics in 2008 after a decade at Neurocrine, and built it into the maker of Palsonify (paltusotine), an FDA-approved oral acromegaly drug. Vertex agreed to buy Crinetics for ~$10B ($85/share) in July 2026, its largest-ever deal, closing Sept 1, 2026. His post-close role was not found.
interesting_fact: The Vertex deal (about $10B, roughly a 100% premium) was the largest acquisition in Vertex's history, and paid out a company Struthers co-founded with three fellow scientists in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Crinetics he co-founded ScienceMedia, an e-learning company for the life sciences and higher-ed markets, and did his doctoral research at the Salk Institute. At Neurocrine he launched the oral non-peptide GnRH antagonist program that produced elagolix. He was elected to the BIO board in March 2026.
notes: Crinetics is now a Vertex company; corporate press routes likely via Vertex media relations. Also co-founded the San Diego Entrepreneurs Exchange (nonprofit for early-stage startups) - good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Post-acquisition title unconfirmed.

name: Alexandre Weinstein Manieu
current_role: Chairman of the Board and ~30% shareholder, Pluri Inc. (Nasdaq/TASE: PLUR); President, Sofgen Pharma (formerly Procaps Group)
profile: Chilean pharma entrepreneur (usually spelled Alejandro Esteban Weinstein Manieu) who ran CFR Pharmaceuticals as CEO from 2000 to 2014, expanding it to 26 countries before its US$3.3B sale to Abbott. Now Switzerland-based, he invests in health/biotech: he put US$6.5M into Israeli cell-technology firm Pluri in 2025 and became its chairman in Dec 2025, and regained control of Procaps (now Sofgen Pharma) in 2024.
interesting_fact: He built CFR from a local Chilean drugmaker into a family pharma group present in 26 countries on three continents, which Abbott bought for about US$3.3 billion.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a board member of Project Blue, an effort to build a small space telescope to directly image an Earth-like planet around Alpha Centauri, and was an International Council member of Harvard's Belfer Center. He also helped set up Chilean stem-cell banks Vidacel and Banco de Vida.
notes: Input name 'Alexandre' is a variant; he is Alejandro Weinstein. Low public/social-media profile; best route is via Pluri IR or Sofgen. Lives in Switzerland and is a GP at PE/VC firms investing in US, Israel and Europe (per Belfer bio). Web search quota ran out mid-research; Pluri press email not verified.

name: Michael D. Hsu
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Kimberly-Clark Corporation; director, McDonald's Corporation
profile: Consumer-goods operator who has been Kimberly-Clark CEO since 2019 and chairman since 2020, after joining as Group President North America in 2013 from Kraft Foods (EVP & Chief Commercial Officer) and H.J. Heinz. On Nov 2, 2026 he closed K-C's acquisition of Kenvue (Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine), creating a ~$32B consumer health and wellness company.
interesting_fact: The Kenvue deal combined Huggies/Kleenex maker Kimberly-Clark with J&J's former consumer-health arm, uniting 10 billion-dollar brands; Hsu called it 'a defining moment in Kimberly-Clark's 154-year history.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Kimberly-Clark he ran Heinz's Foodservice business (2006-08) and Kraft's Grocery unit (2008-10); K-C's board cites his experience 'building and restoring global consumer brands at Ore-Ida and Kraft Grocery.' He also served on Texas Instruments' board (2020-23).
notes: Fortune-500 CEO; route via K-C Media Relations (Kyrsten Aspegren). stockholders@kcc.com is the proxy's stockholder-communications address, not personal. Very busy post-Kenvue integration.

name: Krishna Srinivasan
current_role: Founding Partner, LiveOak Venture Partners (Austin); director, CS Disco (DISCO, NYSE: LAW)
profile: Austin venture capitalist who has backed early-stage Texas tech companies since 2000, first as a partner at Austin Ventures (2000-10) and since 2012 as co-founder of LiveOak Venture Partners. An early DISCO backer, he has sat on its board since 2013 and was its non-executive chair at the 2021 IPO (chair until May 2024). Earlier he wrote supply-chain optimization software at Motorola.
interesting_fact: He has climbed Mount Kilimanjaro and trekked to Everest Base Camp, and wrote a post titled 'Ten Lessons on Entrepreneurship from Summiting Mt. Kilimanjaro.'
deep_cut_fact: He is an IIT Madras mechanical engineer who started out writing large-scale optimization software for supply-chain planning at Motorola (and worked at chip consortium SEMATECH); he was a Palmer Scholar at Wharton. He chairs the board of Austin PBS and is on the board of The Miracle Foundation.
notes: VC - very reachable and relevant for an entrepreneurship podcast (Texas startup ecosystem). Work email is published on his firm's team page (read via fetch tool; page blocks curl).

name: Anthony Digiandomenico
current_role: Co-founder, Head of New Venture Discovery and director, MDB Capital Holdings (Public Ventures); director of ClearSign Technologies and eXoZymes (formerly Invizyne)
profile: Co-founded MDB Capital Group (now Public Ventures) in 1997 with Christopher Marlett, a firm that finances and takes early-stage, IP-driven technology companies public. He holds Class B control shares in MDB Capital Holdings and sits on boards of MDB-launched companies including combustion-tech firm ClearSign, enzyme-biomanufacturing company eXoZymes and ENDRA Life Sciences.
interesting_fact: ClearSign, where he is a director, develops technology to cut NOx emissions from industrial burners and boilers, an energy-relevant angle for the podcast; MDB's model is to launch patent-rich startups directly onto public markets.
deep_cut_fact: He has backed early-stage 'disruptive technology' companies since co-founding MDB in 1997, and sat on the boards of Provention Bio (Jan 2017-May 2020) and Cue Biopharma (2016-19). He holds a Berkeley Haas MBA and a BS in Finance from the University of Colorado.
notes: Low public profile. The only published email found is ClearSign's outside IR firm (for ClearSign investor questions), not MDB. MDB's websites (mdb.com) block automated fetches; web search quota was exhausted so no MDB press email verified.

name: Timothy Spence
current_role: Chair, CEO and President, Fifth Third Bancorp
profile: Banker-strategist who joined Fifth Third in 2015 as Chief Strategy Officer from consultancy Oliver Wyman, ran its consumer bank, payments and digital units, became President in 2020 and CEO in 2022 (later also Chair). He led the Comerica acquisition, which expanded Fifth Third into Texas and the Southwest and added Comerica's middle-market franchise.
interesting_fact: Fifth Third's board credits him with executing the Comerica deal, which it calls the largest U.S. bank acquisition of 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He came to banking from consulting: before Fifth Third he was a Senior Partner at Oliver Wyman, and as Fifth Third's Chief Strategy Officer and Head of Payments, Strategy and Digital Solutions he led the bank's digital transformation and its MB Financial merger.
notes: Q3 2026 earnings release lists media contact Jennifer Hendricks Sullivan and investor contact Matt Curoe (corporate phone lines only, no email) - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/35527/000003552726000229/q32026earningsrelease.htm. Large-bank CEO; route via corporate communications.

profile: Technologist and Niantic co-founder/CTO who helped build the location-based AR platform behind Ingress and Pokemon Go, and spoke publicly on Niantic's AR and Real World Platform. name: Jochen Engert
current_role: Co-founder and Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Flix SE (FlixBus/FlixTrain); business angel
profile: German entrepreneur (b. 1977) who co-founded FlixBus in 2011 with Daniel Krauss and André Schwämmlein when Germany liberalised long-distance bus travel. He was co-CEO of FlixMobility from founding until March 2022, drove its US expansion from 2017 (incl. Greyhound), and since April 2022 has been deputy chair of Flix SE's supervisory board while angel-investing in tech start-ups.
interesting_fact: The founders spotted FlixBus in 2011 when the government planned to end Deutsche Bahn's 75-year monopoly on domestic long-distance travel; they initially held back, assuming 'Deutsche Bahn will surely do it itself.'
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Goßmannsdorf am Main, a ~1,000-person village near Ochsenfurt in Lower Franconia, played in the local football club, studied technical business administration in Stuttgart (with two semesters at the University of Ottawa) and was on a BCG sabbatical writing a PhD on 'Industrial Service Pricing' at WHU when FlixBus began.
notes: Mentors young founders via Startup Teens and is a jury member for BCG's Business@School initiative - good entrepreneurship-podcast angle. No longer operational at Flix; Flix press office is the best documented route. US press: press@FlixBus.com (https://www.flixbus.com/company/press-room).

name: René Lacerte
current_role: Founder, CEO and Board Chair, BILL Holdings (NYSE: BILL)
profile: Serial fintech founder who started BILL (Bill.com) in 2006 to automate small-business payables/receivables, took it public in 2019 and expanded via the Divvy, Invoice2go and Finmark acquisitions; it now serves nearly half a million businesses. Previously he co-founded online payroll company PayCycle (CEO 1999-2005; sold to Intuit in 2009). He is now repositioning BILL as an 'AI native' finance platform.
interesting_fact: In BILL's Nov 2026 results he highlighted AI-driven product velocity: 'five new launches this quarter, and a Visa pilot built in four weeks.'
deep_cut_fact: Before founding companies he was a Group Product Manager at Intuit (1994-99), where he launched Intuit's first connected payroll product and built its bill-payment and credit-card businesses into multi-million-dollar operations. He holds both a BA in Economics and an MS in Industrial Engineering from Stanford.
notes: Press contact named in releases: Lauren Johns. Founder of a public fintech - good fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. corpsec@hq.bill.com is the corporate secretary address in the 2026 proxy.

name: Huh Min
current_role: Founder of WeMakePrice and Neople; investor (current operating title not confirmed)
profile: South Korean entrepreneur (Hur/Heo Min, b. 1976, Busan) who co-founded game studio Neople with five friends in 2001; its 2005 hit Dungeon & Fighter made his fortune when he sold stakes to NHN (2006) and Nexon (2008). In 2010 he founded e-commerce company WeMakePrice (stepped down as CEO in 2013). He later owned baseball teams, including founding the independent Goyang Wonders.
interesting_fact: After getting rich he went to the US, learned the knuckleball from Hall-of-Famer Phil Niekro, and in 2013 signed as a pitcher with the Rockland Boulders of the independent Can-Am League (No. 23), earning his first win in May 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He pitched for Seoul National University's baseball team, was SNU's first student-council president from outside the activist movement, and also studied at Berklee College of Music. His Goyang Wonders (2011-14), managed by Kim Sung-keun, sent 22 cast-off players into KBO pro clubs.
notes: Very private; no published personal contact found. Avoid WeMakePrice topic: the platform collapsed in the 2024 TMON/WeMakePrice settlement crisis, and he faced criticism over meddling as Kiwoom Heroes board chair (2019-21). Gaming/entrepreneur angle is the positive hook. Web search quota exhausted; current role unverified.
